question: Which layer owns specialization (version identity, context keys, budgets, traversal) — and can the residualization stack's three independent traversals become one? Ranked above: whether abc-opt residue should be function-wide or per-version, and whether the portable-C sink survives.
evidence: .ralphi/optimizer-residual-redesign/experiments/1-rederive.md (derivation from CONTRACT, ownership audit with citations, projections, measurement plan)
src/optimize.c:57-118 vs src/residual_analysis.c:24-85 — formatting-only duplicate SCC call-graph; the shared owner exists and is tested but abc-opt does not use it
src/symbolic.c:553-578 with callers src/residualize.c:822-826 and src/residual_builder.c:2684 — per-function DFS giving O(F·(V+E)) preparation and unknown-call facts outside the SCC pass
src/residualize.c:440-463 vs src/residual_builder.c:2047-2110 — duplicated block-leader discovery that has already drifted (end guards, loop headers, TCALL backedges)
src/residualize.c:408-438 + src/symbolic.c:45-75 vs src/residual_builder.c:851-978 — two implementations of context-key canonicalization, family budget and recursion widening
src/optimize.c:361-387 and src/symbolic.h:6-9 — abc-opt walks whole paths (≤4096 leaves/function, ~4.2 KB DagTree per leaf) instead of bounded block versions
REFACTOR.md:811 — documented version-budget divergence (10 versions at one PC vs approved 8 per original PC) as the consequence of policy having no single owner
docs/symbolic-vm.md and docs/threaded-execution.md — one symbolic semantics driving peer sinks; threaded/native already show the correct binding shape
No timings run; all costs are labelled structural projections with a fixture-based measurement plan
decision: Adopt the candidate in ARCHITECTURE.md: five concepts with one owner each — module facts (leaders, call graph, SCC/recursion, unknown calls), symbolic machine, context key policy, version (pc,key,owning residual function), binding. One sink-agnostic driver owns traversal, join materialization, queue order and the canonical-generic fallback; sinks own only residue (native: none; C: per-version residual.asdl block; ABC: per-version bytecode + locally scheduled DAG). Q4 and Q5 are answered yes on evidence (fold module facts and key policy into the core; no policy content, pure duplication). Named deletion set recorded: abc-opt call-graph copy + ArgumentFact fixpoint + path-tree walk, residual_analysis.c as a separate owner, symbolic.c DFS helpers, and the private drivers/leader discovery/key canonicalization in residualize.c and residual_builder.c. Q1 (abc-opt adopting block versions) is surfaced as a version-policy hard gate rather than decided; Q2 (which version-budget policy is authoritative) and Q3 (portable-C scope) are also open.
next: Settle Q1 with evidence: measure interpreter dispatch and optimized-module size on the existing optimizer fixture corpus for shared (versioned) ABC blocks versus the duplicated path tree, and confirm the ABC encoding/verifier permits multiple versions of a non-entry block. Also verify the claim that per-version residue can keep abc-opt's motivating canonicalization (CGET.A 0; MULC.A 0; CGET.B 1; MULC.B 1; ADD.A; RET) without a function-wide DAG, and that idempotence/byte-determinism hold under the versioned sink.
